title: Semantic-aware KV compaction, adaptive request pacing, and micro-model fallback orchestration for OOM avoidance
creator: Avery Chen
description: Background: We continue to see transient OOMs during high-concurrency continuous batching with wide-context requests. Existing LRU-style eviction and coarse batch admission cause tail latencies and frequent fallback spikes. Proposal: Implement a coordinated three-part system to reduce OOM incidence without large quality regressions: (1) semantic-aware KV compaction that computes a low-cost semantic importance score per KV entry and compacts/merges low-value entries instead of evicting whole segments; (2) adaptive request pacing / micro-throttling at the batch-admission layer that uses predicted slot occupancy and per-request priority to delay low-priority requests by a few ms rather than hard rejection; (3) a micro-model fallback orchestrator that transparently routes affected requests to a compact quantized model variant when memory headroom is insufficient, with quality-aware hedging and retry logic.
acceptance_criteria: >= 65% reduction in transient OOM events on high-load test harness compared to baseline
No more than 3% quality regression on our prompt set (evaluated per-model) when micro-model fallback is exercised
P99 latency increase <= 10% for routed requests under normal load
Telemetry shows correct attribution: compaction vs pacing vs fallback decisions
proposal:
High-level design:

1) Semantic-aware KV compaction
- Compute a compact embedding or locality hash for KV entries at insertion time (approximate, cheap) and maintain a rolling 'semantic salience' score combining recency, access frequency, and embedding novelty.
- When memory pressure threshold is reached, perform compaction: merge nearby/low-salience KV slices into a compressed snapshot that preserves prefix decoding paths but reduces memory by factor ~2-4 depending on quantization profile. Compaction should be incremental and performed on GPU when possible, otherwise asynchronously offload to host.
- Maintain compaction metadata so subsequent lookups can reconstruct or rehydrate only hot fragments.

2) Adaptive request pacing
- Extend batch-admission to predict occupancy using recent active KV working set and inflight token count (fast estimator). If predicted occupancy exceeds soft threshold, apply sub-ms pacing to low-priority requests (PB-level priority inferred from route/tenant/headers). Pacing is implemented as a delayed enqueue rather than rejection to preserve streaming semantics.
- Pacing thresholds are dynamically tuned by an online controller that observes OOM rate and mean slot occupancy.

3) Micro-model fallback orchestrator
- Register compact quantized model variants as validated fallbacks for each heavy model. Fallback orchestrator decides to route either whole request to fallback or to split: attempt original path with extended compaction + pacing, and if OOM occurs, transparently retry on fallback with token-level hedging if needed.
- Retries must be idempotent at the request level; preserve function-call semantics by switching to a hedged mode rather than blind retry.

Trade-offs and rationale:
- Semantic compaction avoids wholesale eviction which causes large quality regressions; it costs CPU/GPU cycles to compute compaction metadata but reduces eviction churn.
- Pacing adds small latency to lower-priority traffic but prevents large cascades of OOMs that affect high-priority traffic.
- Fallback models incur some quality drop; hedging guarantees reduce user-visible regressions while keeping availability high.
implementation_notes: Kernel changes: add compact-merge operator in runtime; reuse existing KV snapshot APIs where possible
Admission changes: implement fast occupancy estimator; add per-request priority tag in ingress path
Fallback: expose routing hooks in smart-routing layer; add canary traffic flag for early trials
Storage: compacted KV artifacts stored in per-GPU slot ephemeral arena with async rehydrate path
Backwards compatibility: feature flag controlled, default off in prod until canary
rollout_plan: 1) Internal load test (dev cluster) with synthetic workload matching 95th percentile of customer distribution; enable semantic compaction only. 2) Enable pacing for low-priority routes in staging; observe OOM and latency metrics. 3) Register and smoke-test micro-model fallbacks in canary (1% traffic) with end-to-end telemetry. 4) Gradually ramp to 10% then 50% and monitor quality/regressions; if metrics pass, enable globally behind runtime-1.20 rollout.
